fit: Pinta sprout extract and rat melatonin biomarker
assessment: In Experiment 1, fasted rats given Pinta sprout extract had plasma melatonin about 16% higher than the chow control and 2.9 times the fasting group at 90 minutes. Neither sleep behavior nor insomnia was measured. The treatment was an extract from sprouted beans, with no boiled-pinto or Parkinson comparison.

fit: student sleep-quality cross-section with legume preference
assessment: Table 2 OR 1.59 (95% CI 1.22 to 2.08) refers to dislike of grouped beans, chickpeas and lentils. The pooled rice, pasta or beans meal item cannot identify pinto or an isolated ingestion effect. The study does not test Parkinson insomnia.

fit: parallel bean and sleep measures with fecal bacterial comparisons
assessment: Tables 3 and 4 compare fecal Akkermansia with sleep category and canary bean frequency separately. Supplement S1 names no pinto and gives no bean-by-sleep or preparation data. The older-adult cohort does not establish a Parkinson-specific insomnia effect.

fit: injected nutmeg extract and mouse locomotion from original abstract
assessment: The 1984 author abstract reports moderate reduction in spontaneous activity and separate effects on ethanol and amphetamine activity comparisons. The accessible endpoint is locomotion, with no separate rest-tremor measure and no oral culinary or Parkinson comparison. Original methods and figures remain open.

fit: ground nutmeg poisoning and intention tremor with uncertain report overlap
assessment: Both original accounts describe intention tremor after excess powdered nutmeg. Shared authors, setting, age and time course make the same case plausible. Ingestion details and medication history conflict. The 2017 report includes diazepam co-ingestion and a positive benzodiazepine test, leaving causal attribution and Parkinson rest-tremor effects unresolved.
